skill.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skill.description: Guides AI coding assistants through final branch integration with test checks, merge options, pull request creation, and cleanup choices.
skill.summary: Finish a development branch with tests, Git integration choices, and cleanup safeguards.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences around Git and test examples, not Ruby backtick execution. The remaining confirmed issues are unsafe unquoted command substitution in the worktree check and conflicting pull request cleanup guidance. The skill is useful, but the author should fix shell quoting and align cleanup instructions before broad publication.

remediation.suggestion: Store the current branch in a variable, quote it, and pass it to grep with fixed-string matching and option delimiters.

remediation.issue: Conflicting worktree cleanup instructions for pull requests
remediation.suggestion: Choose one Option 2 behavior, then align Step 4, Step 5, the quick reference, and common mistakes.

remediation.issue: Shell examples rely on placeholder replacement
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to quote generated titles, branch names, and paths before running shell commands. Prefer argument arrays when tools support them.

content.value_statement: Finishing branch work often leaves unclear choices about merge, pull request, cleanup, or discard. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured completion workflow.
actual_capabilities: Verifies project tests before presenting branch completion options.
Helps identify a likely base branch with common Git checks.
Presents four choices: local merge, pull request, keep branch, or discard.
Provides command sequences for merge, PR creation, branch deletion, and worktree removal.
Requires typed confirmation before the discard path.
Lists common mistakes and red flags for final branch handling.
limitations: Does not determine project-specific test commands automatically.
Assumes Git is available, and PR creation assumes GitHub CLI is available.
Contains inconsistent guidance about worktree cleanup after creating a pull request.
Shell examples need careful quoting when replacing placeholders.

use_cases.title: Complete a feature branch
use_cases.description: Run final tests, choose a merge path, and clean up local branch state after implementation work is done.

use_cases.title: Prepare a pull request
use_cases.description: Push a finished branch and create a concise PR with a summary and test plan.

use_cases.title: Resolve worktree state
use_cases.description: Decide whether to preserve, remove, or discard a worktree after a branch reaches completion.

prompt_templates.title: Finish my branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the finishing-a-development-branch skill. Tests are ready to run, and I need clear options for completing this branch.

prompt_templates.title: Create a PR
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the finishing-a-development-branch skill. Verify tests, push this branch, and prepare a pull request summary and test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Merge locally
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the finishing-a-development-branch skill. Verify tests, identify the base branch, and guide me through a local merge.

prompt_templates.title: Audit completion options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the finishing-a-development-branch skill. Compare merge, PR, keep, and discard paths for this repository before changing branch state.

output_examples.input: Implementation is complete and tests have not been run yet.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs or requests the project test command first, then stops if failures appear before offering integration options.

output_examples.input: Tests pass and I want to create a pull request.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the branch path, pushes the branch, drafts a PR summary, and reports the chosen cleanup behavior.

output_examples.input: I want to discard this branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists the branch, commits, and worktree that would be removed, then waits for exact typed confirmation.

best_practices: Run tests before offering merge, PR, keep, or discard options.
Ask for explicit confirmation before any destructive branch or worktree action.
Quote branch names, paths, and generated text before using shell commands.
anti_patterns: Merging or creating a PR while tests are failing.
Deleting a branch or worktree without a clear confirmation step.
Changing cleanup behavior for pull requests without telling the user.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an AI coding assistant finish branch work through tests, merge choices, PR creation, and cleanup decisions.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to run the project test suite, but the correct command depends on the repository.

faq.question: Can it create a pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a GitHub CLI flow for pushing a branch and creating a pull request.

faq.question: Can it delete work?
faq.answer: Yes, the discard path can delete a branch and worktree. The skill requires exact typed confirmation first.

faq.question: Is it limited to GitHub?
faq.answer: The PR example uses GitHub CLI. The merge and cleanup guidance applies to standard Git repositories.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publishing?
faq.answer: They should align the pull request cleanup guidance and quote shell values in command examples.
